 Dated this the 6th day of April, 2018  JUDGMENT

The petitioners have approached this Court aggrieved by Ext.P32 order of the Secretary of the respondent Panchayat, which has been affirmed in Ext.P34 minutes of the meeting of the respondent Panchayat, that endorses the views of the Secretary.

The facts in the writ petition would indicate that, against an order passed against the petitioners refusing to renew their Dangerous and Offensive (D & O) licence for units engaged in the manufacture of packaged drinking water and soda, the petitioners had approached this Court through W.P(C).No.16914 of 2017.

The said writ petition was disposed by Ext.P29 judgment, wherein this Court directed the Panchayat to consider the request of the petitioners for renewal of licence to their units, afresh, in accordance with law,
making it clear that the petitioner should comply with the conditions imposed in various permissions granted to them and would operate the unit only in strict compliance with the conditions imposed by the local authority.

It is the case of the petitioner that although Ext.P32 order passed by the Secretary is in purported compliance with the directions in Ext.P29 judgment, the said judgment had directed the Panchayat, and not the Secretary, to take the decision.

It is therefore,
stated that Ext.P32 order of the Secretary is without jurisdiction and Ext.P34 minutes of the Panchayat, which affirms the decision of the Secretary cannot be said to be a decision taken pursuant to Ext.P29.

2. I have heard the learned Senior counsel Sri.S.Sreekumar duly assisted by Sri.C.P.Peethamparan appearing for the petitioners, Sri.K.N.Abilash for the respondent Panchayat and also the learned counsel for respondents.
The learned counsel for the respondent Panchayat would submit that the Panchayat has no objection in taking a fresh decision in the matter based on the directions in Ext.P29 judgment.

Taking note of the said submission of the learned counsel for the respondent Panchayat, I quash Ext.P32 order of the Secretary and Ext.P34 minutes of the Panchayat to the extent it affirms the Unknown vs Present on 7 April, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132260182/
6 decision of the Secretary in Ext.P32, and direct the respondent Panchayat to take fresh decision in the matter, after hearing the petitioners and others likely to be affected by orders to be passed,
within three weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

I make it clear that in the event of the petitioners making a requests before the respondent Panchayat for the latter's presence in their premises for the purposes of closing one of the bore wells and complying with the directions in Ext.P29 judgment, the respondent Panchayat shall depute an authorised person to oversee the said activity.
The writ petition is thus disposed as above.

Sd/-
A.K.JAYASANKARAN NAMBIAR JUDGE mns/06.04.18 Unknown vs Present on 7 April, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132260182/
